entries.name: dash
entries.summary: A rich terminal dashboard for pull requests, issues, and notifications.
entries.best_for: Maintainers who live in PR, issue, and notification queues.
entries.avoid_if: You prefer one-off commands over a persistent TUI.

entries.name: pr-review
entries.summary: View, navigate, reply to, and resolve PR review threads.
entries.best_for: Reviewers who want inline PR review workflows in the terminal.
entries.avoid_if: Your team reviews exclusively in the GitHub web UI.

entries.name: notify
entries.summary: Display GitHub notifications in the terminal.
entries.best_for: Developers who want notification awareness without the browser.
entries.avoid_if: You already manage notifications through email or mobile.

entries.name: pr-review
entries.summary: View, navigate, reply to, and resolve PR review threads.
entries.best_for: Reviewers who want inline PR review workflows in the terminal.
entries.avoid_if: Your team reviews exclusively in the GitHub web UI.

entries.name: stack
entries.summary: Manage stacked pull requests on GitHub.
entries.best_for: Teams that split large changes into dependent PRs.
entries.avoid_if: Your team avoids stacked changes.

entries.name: dependabot
entries.summary: Review Dependabot pull requests from GitHub CLI.
entries.best_for: Teams that process many dependency update pull requests.
entries.avoid_if: You do not use Dependabot.

entries.name: enhance
entries.summary: A fast terminal UI for inspecting and managing GitHub Actions.
entries.best_for: Developers who want an interactive terminal UI for GitHub Actions workflows.
entries.avoid_if: You only need basic workflow status output or prefer the GitHub web UI.

entries.name: workflow-stats
entries.summary: Calculate workflow and job success rate and execution time.
entries.best_for: CI owners investigating slow or flaky workflows.
entries.avoid_if: You only need the latest run status.

entries.name: actions-importer
entries.summary: Plan and automate migrations into GitHub Actions.
entries.best_for: Enterprise teams migrating from other CI systems.
entries.avoid_if: Your project is already on GitHub Actions.

entries.name: aw
entries.summary: Run GitHub agentic workflows from the CLI.
entries.best_for: Developers experimenting with GitHub-native agent workflows.
entries.avoid_if: You are not using agentic automation yet.

entries.name: models
entries.summary: Use GitHub Models from GitHub CLI.
entries.best_for: Developers testing prompts and models from the terminal.
entries.avoid_if: You do not use GitHub Models.

entries.name: mcp
entries.summary: Run GitHub MCP Server using existing GitHub CLI authentication.
entries.best_for: Users connecting AI tools to GitHub through MCP.
entries.avoid_if: You do not use MCP-compatible clients.

entries.name: poi
entries.summary: Safely clean up local branches.
entries.best_for: Developers who want a trustworthy branch cleanup default.
entries.avoid_if: You want to manually inspect every branch before deletion.

entries.name: branch
entries.summary: Fuzzy find, switch between, and delete branches.
entries.best_for: Developers with many local branches.
entries.avoid_if: You want only automated cleanup rather than manual selection.

entries.name: install
entries.summary: Install GitHub release binaries interactively.
entries.best_for: Developers who often install tools from GitHub releases.
entries.avoid_if: You already use a package manager for all release binaries.

entries.name: markdown-preview
entries.summary: Preview Markdown as it appears on GitHub.
entries.best_for: README, issue template, and documentation review.
entries.avoid_if: You need fully offline preview support.

entries.name: gfm-preview
entries.summary: Preview GitHub-flavored Markdown, including offline workflows.
entries.best_for: Writers who need Markdown preview without relying on GitHub web UI.
entries.avoid_if: You only need the simplest browser-based preview.

entries.name: s
entries.summary: Interactively search GitHub repositories.
entries.best_for: Finding repositories quickly from a terminal workflow.
entries.avoid_if: You need advanced code search rather than repository search.

entries.name: grep
entries.summary: Print matching lines from repositories through the GitHub API.
entries.best_for: Searching repository content without cloning.
entries.avoid_if: You need local ripgrep speed across checked-out code.

entries.name: find-code
entries.summary: Search GitHub code with fzf.
entries.best_for: Developers who want interactive code search from the terminal.
entries.avoid_if: You need local search inside a checked-out repository.

entries.name: sbom
entries.summary: Generate software bills of materials with GitHub CLI.
entries.best_for: Teams that need SBOM output during release or compliance work.
entries.avoid_if: Your SBOM workflow is already handled by another build step.

entries.name: token
entries.summary: Create installation access tokens for GitHub Apps.
entries.best_for: Developers working with GitHub App authentication.
entries.avoid_if: You only use personal access tokens or browser flows.

entries.name: gei
entries.summary: Support GitHub Enterprise Importer migration workflows.
entries.best_for: Enterprise teams migrating repositories to GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
entries.avoid_if: You are not running GitHub migration projects.
